items.topic: Prerequisite: swarm-manager initiatives HTTP API surface
items.context: Round 1 d3 resolved to 'API-to-API via api-core/discovery package' (the operator's freeform). Discovery returns a base URL, then the caller speaks plain HTTP. Today swarm-manager exposes runs/tasks/profiles over HTTP but has NO initiatives HTTP endpoints — initiatives is CLI-only (verified via codebase scan). The auto-create plan therefore depends on first exposing an initiatives endpoint. Where does that work live?

options.label: Bundle the initiatives HTTP endpoint into this item's Phase 1
options.rationale: One item, one shippable end-to-end behavior. The endpoint is small (POST /api/v1/initiatives mirroring the CLI's create flags) and there is no other consumer queued, so splitting buys nothing. Recommended because the operator's stated goal ('one CLI call') is unreachable without this, and a separate prerequisite ticket adds sequencing friction without simplifying review.

options.label: Split into a prerequisite execute item: 'swarm-manager: expose initiatives over HTTP'
options.rationale: Cleaner separation of concerns; the HTTP surface becomes reusable and reviewable on its own. Costs: a second item to schedule, a hard dependency edge, and this item blocks until the prerequisite ships. Use only if the HTTP surface turns out non-trivial (auth, pagination, list/get/update parity).

options.label: Skip API-to-API entirely; have prompt-manager shell out to `swarm-manager initiatives create` CLI
options.rationale: Cheapest. Reuses existing CLI as the seam. But this contradicts d3 (operator chose API-to-API), couples prompt-manager to a binary on PATH, and is hostile to UI usage. Listed for completeness only.

items.topic: Where the auto-create call executes: prompt-manager API server vs prompt-manager CLI
items.context: Once an HTTP initiatives endpoint exists (d6), there are two natural homes for the cross-scenario call. Server-side keeps the API as the single source of truth for the operator's intent (UI and CLI both inherit the behavior). Client-side keeps prompt-manager's API process free of cross-scenario network dependencies.

options.label: Server-side: prompt-manager API's decision-accept handler invokes swarm-manager initiatives via discovery
options.rationale: Single behavioral source of truth — UI, CLI, and any future API client all auto-create identically. Matches the three-surface parity rule (a CLI-only orchestration would diverge from UI). Failure surfaces in the API response so all surfaces render it the same way. Recommended because boundary-of-responsibility belongs at the API, not at each client.

options.label: Client-side: prompt-manager CLI calls decision-accept, then calls swarm-manager API directly on success
options.rationale: Keeps prompt-manager API free of swarm-manager runtime dependency. But UI would have to re-implement the same orchestration to match, violating parity; failure semantics also diverge per surface.

items.topic: Retry mechanism when auto-create failed (per d4: decision still accepts, create may fail)
items.context: Round 1 d4 chose 'decision still accepts; structured warning; record auto_create_status'. That implies a retry path. d5 chose 'error on accept if metadata missing', so retries here only cover the create-side failure (duplicate name, validation, transient outage). What is the retry shape?

options.label: New CLI subcommand `prompt-manager team decision-retry-auto-create <decision-id>` (and equivalent API endpoint)
options.rationale: Explicit, idempotent, scriptable. Mirrors how heartbeat/initiative retries are typically modeled. Reads `auto_create_status` on the decision, refuses if status is 'created', re-derives the payload, calls swarm-manager, updates status. Recommended because it makes the retry a first-class operator action rather than a hidden side effect.

options.label: Overload `decision-accept --retry-auto-create` (no separate command)
options.rationale: Smaller surface area. Risk: 'accept' on an already-accepted decision is otherwise rejected — would need a special path that confuses the accept contract.

options.label: No retry command; operator just runs `swarm-manager initiatives create` manually after a failure and updates auto_create_status with `decision-update`
options.rationale: Re-introduces the exact pain this item is solving (hand-transcription) on the failure path. Fine as a Phase-1 stopgap if d6=B splits the work.

options.label: Auto-retry with exponential backoff inside the API handler before returning
options.rationale: Hides transient failures, but blocks decision-accept response on swarm-manager availability and offers no recovery for non-transient errors (validation). Worse on every dimension that matters here.

items.notes: Should instruct on how to do this in the cli output. So operator sees error + workaround

items.topic: CLI output / observability shape on decision-accept when auto-create fires
items.context: Operator note on round-1 d2: 'Make sure the cli output makes it clear that an initiative was auto-created, gives command/location/etc. to find it. Also remind to add more details/depends_on/etc. as needed.' This decision picks the concrete output shape to encode that requirement.

options.label: Structured 'Auto-Created Initiative' block with name, priority, depends_on, get-command, edit-command, and a 'Reminder:' line for follow-up edits
options.rationale: Matches the operator's note precisely: clear creation indicator + lookup commands + edit nudge. Renders identically in the UI's accept-success view. Failure case renders the same block with `Status: failed (<reason>)` + the retry command from d8. Recommended because it operationalizes the operator's stated need without ambiguity.

options.label: One-line 'Created initiative <name>' summary; full details only via `--verbose`
options.rationale: Cleaner default. But the operator explicitly asked for command/location guidance and the follow-up reminder, both of which would be hidden without a flag — re-introducing friction.

items.text: Codebase scan confirms the seam shape: `github.com/vrooli/api-core/discovery` exposes `ResolveScenarioURLDefault(ctx, scenarioName) (string, error)` returning a base URL; callers then issue raw HTTP. prompt-manager already uses this pattern (`resolvePromptManagerBaseURL` for skills endpoints) and workspace-sandbox uses it for sandboxing — so this item adopts an established pattern, not a new one. Critical caveat: swarm-manager's HTTP server today exposes profiles/tasks/runs/runners/investigation under /api/v1/* but NOT initiatives — initiatives is CLI-only. d6 above forces a decision on whether to add that endpoint inside this item or as a prerequisite split.

Pre-accept mutability of `initiative_metadata` is intentionally permissive: `decision-update` may set/replace the block any number of times before first accept (consistent with F15 modifications). The immutability rule fires only post-accept. This is implicit in the plan but not explicitly stated; round-2 plan revision adds a one-line note to the Validation Policy section so executors don't over-restrict the write path.

plan_updates: Updated plan to (a) fold the five round-1 decisions into firm commitments (replaced 'Open Decisions' with 'Resolved Decisions'), (b) record the d3=Other resolution as concrete api-core/discovery seam wiring in Phase 3, (c) flag the missing swarm-manager initiatives HTTP endpoint as a new Phase-0 prerequisite (pending d6), (d) expand Phase 3 with the d2-notes-driven CLI output spec (pending d9), (e) add an `auto_create_status` field to the decision schema and stub a retry path (pending d8), (f) clarify pre-accept mutability in Validation Policy, (g) tighten Risks with the new cross-scenario HTTP-availability item, and (h) add a 'Round 2 Open Questions' section listing d6-d9 explicitly so executors don't lose them.
